title: Neural Network Engine
description: A feedforward network built from raw NumPy — every gradient computed and checked by hand.
question: Could I build a modular neural network framework using only NumPy — while understanding every line — instead of importing PyTorch?
journey: I wanted to know what backpropagation actually computes, not just what it's called. So the rule was simple: no autograd, no framework — every gradient derived and written by hand.
The engine ended up with dense layers, He initialization, SGD and Adam optimizers, and a softmax cross-entropy loss built from the definition upward.
It reached 97% accuracy on MNIST. The number mattered less than being able to explain, at every layer, exactly why the loss went down.

title: Early Projects (2020-2022)
description: Archived GitHub. It contains my first experiments from ages 11-13, before rebuilding from first principles. No longer maintained, last significant update was in 2022.
question: What did the first lines of code look like before frameworks, abstraction layers, or formal software engineering?
journey: Between 2020 and 2022, learning wasn't driven by formal roadmaps — it was pure trial, error, and hacking together scripts to see what moved on screen.
This repository holds those initial experiments: early OpenCV gesture loops, basic motor drivers, serial controls, and unpolished automation scripts.
Though long retired and unmaintained, these projects are preserved as a relic of the original spark that led to rebuilding systems from first principles.
